headline: Executive order from 2003 that appears to grant the European Central Bank certain legal privileges and protections in the United States.
what_it_does: Only the title, "European Central Bank," was provided. Orders like this usually name a foreign or international body under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That law can give the body some protection from lawsuits, certain taxes, and searches of its records while it operates in the US. The exact terms are not in the source material.

who_it_affects.group: The European Central Bank and its staff
who_it_affects.how: They may receive legal immunities and tax or customs exemptions when doing business or holding property in the United States.

who_it_affects.group: People and businesses with legal claims against the European Central Bank
who_it_affects.how: They may face limits on suing the bank in US courts.

when_it_takes_effect: Likely upon signing on May 29, 2003; the source material does not state a date.
